title: OpenAI Responses compatibility inventory and runtime mitigation plan
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Purpose: produce a compact, prioritized inventory of concrete behavioral deltas between Redwood's Responses-compatible runtime and the OpenAI Responses API, then define a short-term runtime mitigation surface (shim/fallbacks/translation rules) and a testable rollout plan. This ticket focuses on observable protocol-level differences that affect production customers: streaming chunk semantics, function/tool call lifecycle and metadata, structured output encoding, event ordering, and error/partial-completion behaviors. Outcome: a mitigation patchset + test harness to reduce customer regressions during tenant migrations and model upgrades.
background: We onboarded several customers who expect parity with OpenAI's Responses API for streaming and tool-calling. Customers observed differences in four classes: 1) stream chunk typing and finalization markers, 2) how function call intents are signaled mid-stream and then completed with tool results, 3) structured JSON outputs with schema enforcement and partial chunking, 4) error semantics for interrupted streams and idempotent retry. Existing compatibility reports list gaps but are high level. This ticket creates an actionable inventory and runtime shim design with measurable acceptance criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Comprehensive catalog of at least 18 distinct parity gaps with examples (input, observed Redwood output, expected OpenAI-style output)
A runtime shim design document that maps OpenAI event types to Redwood event types and specifies fallback behaviors for at least streaming and function calling mismatches
Working test harness that can replay recorded OpenAI-style streams and assert Redwood runtime emits compatible events within configured tolerance
Canary rollout plan with metrics and rollback thresholds; one canary on dedicated capacity and one on hosted path
Automated regression tests added to CI for the top 5 highest-risk gaps
tasks: Run delta-capture job across 3 representative models and 4 prompt families to gather empirical examples
Normalize captured traces to canonical event log format and annotate by gap category
Prioritize gaps by customer impact and implementability; produce a top-5 quick-fix list
Design runtime shim that synthesizes missing OpenAI events and normalizes chunk boundaries
Implement unit and integration tests in the responses-compat test harness
Create canary config: 1% traffic on hosted API, 5% on dedicated; monitor defined metrics for 72 hours
Document mapping table and publish to internal Confluence and the SDK team for review
decisions: We will prefer non-invasive runtime shims over protocol-breaking changes to the core serving runtime for the short term
Shim will be opt-out per customer via a header and opt-in for Dedicated upgrades; default enabled for new customers until parity gaps are closed
For function/tool calls, the shim will emit an intermediate 'tool_call_started' event to match OpenAI semantics, then attach tool result as a terminal 'tool_call_result' event
We will not attempt deep semantic alignment (e.g., model tokenization differences) in this ticket; that is delegated to a separate kernel/quantization workstream
risks: Shim adds CPU and memory overhead under high concurrency; must be profiled to avoid SLO regressions
Event synthesis could mask true runtime errors; need end-to-end observability to avoid Silent Failures
Edge-case ordering differences may still cause application-level breakage for tool orchestrators that rely on strict event sequences
Customer expectations may drift if we over-commit to 1:1 parity; ongoing maintenance cost for shim must be budgeted
metrics_and_alerts: compat.latency.p50 and p95: shim-induced p95 increase > 10% requires rollback
toolcall.missing_final_event.rate: any non-zero during canary is a blocker
stream.chunk_reassembly_failures: trend > 0.5% after rollout triggers automated rollback
test_plan: Create recorded OpenAI-style streams (10k traces) covering: streaming-only, streaming+function-call, structured-output-with-schemas, interrupted-streams
Replay harness will assert event type sequence, JSON schema validity, and per-chunk offset semantics
Add fuzz tests that inject arbitrary chunk boundaries to ensure reassembly logic handles misaligned token boundaries
Integrate harness into PR pipeline with a lightweight smoke job and a nightly full regression run
implementation_notes: Mapping rules: map OpenAI 'delta' chunks with 'role' and 'content' keys to Redwood 'chunk' events; include explicit 'final' marker when OpenAI sends a 'done' event
Function calls: attach a stable call_id and ensure tool result is correlated; persist minimal call metadata in request context for retries
Structured output: if Redwood emits partial JSON chunks, shim must attempt streaming-safe reassembly and validate against the declared schema before forwarding
Retries: build idempotency envelope keyed by (request_id, call_id) to dedupe repeated tool results
Telemetry: add a compatibility trace id to each shimmed request for easier correlation across logs and traces
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal dev deployment and run harness against synthetic traces
Phase 1: canary on staging environment for internal customers only (24h) with automatic rollback on metrics breach
Phase 2: 1% traffic on hosted API and a single Dedicated cluster with permissive opt-in for existing customers (72h monitoring)
Phase 3: expand to 10% and gradually to 100% after two stable weeks and sign-off from core SDK and Console teams
